name: Bosentan
route_note: Oral tablet twice daily; dispersible tablets for children
originator: F. Hoffmann-La Roche; developed by Actelion

discovery.note: Non-peptide endothelin receptor antagonist; its developers founded Actelion to bring it to market.

rx_status: prescription (restricted programme for liver and pregnancy risk)
tagline: First oral endothelin receptor antagonist for pulmonary arterial hypertension
summary: Bosentan is an oral antagonist of both endothelin ETA and ETB receptors. It was the first oral therapy approved for pulmonary arterial hypertension and is also used in the EU to reduce new digital ulcers in systemic sclerosis.
mechanism: Endothelin-1 is a potent vasoconstrictor and smooth-muscle mitogen that is overproduced in PAH. Bosentan competitively blocks its binding to ETA and ETB receptors.
This lowers pulmonary vascular resistance, and may limit vascular remodelling, improving exercise capacity and haemodynamics.
uses: Reduction of new digital ulcers in systemic sclerosis (EU)

history.title: Actelion founded
history.detail: Former Roche scientists found Actelion and license bosentan.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: FDA approves Tracleer in November, the first oral PAH therapy.

history.title: Digital ulcers
history.detail: EU approval extended to prevention of digital ulcers in systemic sclerosis.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic bosentan becomes available in the US.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic CYP2C9 and CYP3A4; induces both enzymes

safety.boxed_warning: Risks of hepatotoxicity and embryo-fetal toxicity; available only through a restricted programme (REMS).

facts: Bosentan's development led to the founding of Actelion, later one of Europe's largest biotech companies.
Monthly liver function testing is required during bosentan treatment.
